chunks: From him, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Among the signs of the believer are three: good management in livelihood, patience in the face of calamity, and deep understanding in religion.
And he said: 'There is no good in a man who does not exercise moderation in his livelihood, such that it is suitable for neither his worldly life nor his hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a believer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) links financial prudence (*husn al-taqdir*) directly to spiritual resilience, framing economic moderation as a prerequisite for enduring divine trials with patience. This triad underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating worldly stewardship with deep religious understanding (*taffaqquh*), ensuring that material pursuits serve both temporal stability and eternal success.
